poor-countries-take-the-poison.notes: All checked claims hold. Summers memo: dated 12 December 1991; signed by Summers as chief economist; 'impeccable' sentence; written by Pritchett; both say it was sarcastic; Pritchett says the leak was edited to strip context; leaked 2 February 1992 by Roberto Smeraldi of Friends of the Earth to Jornal do Brasil (Wikipedia); Brazil's environment secretary replied 'Your reasoning is perfectly logical but totally insane' (Grist, added; Wikipedia names Lutzenberger). Probo Koala: night of 19 August 2006 (Amnesty); Amsterdam attempt 2 July 2006, ship left 5 July (Wikipedia); 'newly licensed' Compagnie Tommy and more than 500 tons (Wikipedia); $17,000 (Amnesty, and the card; Wikipedia gives the contract as €18,500, a small discrepancy between sources); more than 100,000 sought treatment, inquiry 15 deaths, court 17 (Al Jazeera); $198m in 2007 without admitting wrongdoing, ending action against it (Wikipedia; Amnesty says 'around US$200 million' and 'sweeping immunity'); £30m to almost 30,000 in 2009 (Wikipedia); Dutch €1m fine on 23 July 2010 for concealing the waste's dangerous nature (BHRRC, Wikipedia; Amnesty misdates it to 2008); Trafigura says the waste 'could not have caused the death and ongoing health concerns' (Wikipedia). 'Without admitting liability' in 2009 was not confirmed word for word on an opened page but matches what the settlement is widely reported as. would_settle is realistic: Basel national reports are public.

carbon-credits-new-land-grab.notes: Confirmed: 'an estimated 167 Ogiek houses, including a school' (Survival); Blue Carbon signed with Kenya in October 2023, told the BBC it did 'not have any ongoing projects in Kenya', and the government says the operations protect the environment (BBC via BHRRC); founded October 2022, chaired by Sheikh Ahmed Dalmook Al Maktoum, Zimbabwe 7.5m ha (~20%), Zambia 8m ha, Tanzania 8m ha of forest reserves, Liberia ~1m ha (~10%) (AFP 2025); Zambia 10% (Down To Earth, CorpWatch); 'the size of the UK' and Liberia 70% 'of the royalties for the first decade' (CorpWatch); NGOs learned of the Liberian MoU 'until government sources leaked the news' (Middle East Eye, added, supports 'leaked'). NRT: more than 2m ha, 14 conservancies, Netflix and Meta among buyers, January 2025 ruling on Cherab and Biliqo Bulesa, about 20% of credits, Verra hold in March 2023 and second suspension in 2025 (REDD-Monitor, Survival); reinstated mid-June 2026 (REDD-Monitor, 23 June 2026). The paragraph 1 statement that Blue Carbon signed its deals 'during 2023' is plausible but no opened page dates every deal. would_settle: carbon registries (Verra, Gold Standard) publish project boundaries, so the overlap count is realistic; government agreements mostly are not published.
